what: Genuine Parts distributes replacement parts. Through NAPA it supplies car parts to repair shops and stores across North America and Europe, and through Motion it supplies bearings, belts and industrial components to factories.
customers: Independent repair garages, NAPA stores, fleet operators, and industrial maintenance teams.
money: NAPA branded distribution in North America, Europe and Australasia
moat: Distribution centres and stores placed so a mechanic or a factory can get a part the same day, which is what customers pay for rather than the lowest price.
risks: Net margin collapsed to near zero after restructuring and legal charges
Industrial demand has been soft and automotive margins compressed
Return on invested capital of about 2% after the charges
opportunities: A dividend yield around 3.5% with a very long record of increases
The average age of vehicles keeps rising, which raises repair demand
Cost reduction programmes are intended to restore margins from a low base
watch: Comparable sales in both segments and whether operating margin recovers.
